channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Reshuffles Security Apparatus Amid Corruption Probe
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has reshuffled Kazakhstan's security apparatus following the arrest of the head of the national wealth fund and the State Railways chief on corruption charges. Key figures, including the KNB chief, were dismissed or sanctioned as the investigation into corrupt activities continues.

item.title: Relatives Appeal Uzbek Scholar's Espionage Conviction in Kazakhstan
item.description: Relatives of Uzbek scholar Iqboljon Qoraboyev are appealing his 10-year espionage sentence in Kazakhstan, handed down after a closed-door trial. Qoraboyev, who taught international relations at a private university in Astana, was convicted under Article 176 of the Kazakh Criminal Code. Details remain scarce.

item.title: Astana Man Sentenced to Over Six Years for Car Dealership Fraud
item.description: A man in Astana has been sentenced to six years and eight months for defrauding car owners. He convinced six individuals to sell their vehicles by falsely claiming loans were approved, resulting in a total loss of over 103 million tenge. The fraud impacted residents of Astana and Karaganda. He is also banned from car sales for six years.

item.title: Internet Fraud Worth 40 Million Tenge Under Investigation in Pavlodar Region
item.description: Four suspects have been detained in the Pavlodar region in connection with a series of internet frauds. Investigators have identified nine victims and estimate the total damage at approximately 40 million tenge. Police are examining the role of each suspect and their potential involvement in other similar crimes, with the number of victims possibly increasing.

item.title: Uzbekistan Explores International Atomic Energy Market Amidst Nuclear Power Plant Construction
item.description: Uzbekistan's industrial sector is poised to enter the international atomic energy market through its nuclear power plant construction. To achieve this, domestic enterprises must develop production and technological capabilities aligned with international standards and client requirements. This was discussed at the 'World Atomic Days' forum in Antalya, where local contractor readiness was emphasized.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to open 74 polling stations abroad for upcoming presidential election
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has established 74 polling stations in 33 countries for its upcoming presidential election, aiming to ensure citizen participation abroad. The number of stations may increase before election day. Voters can cast ballots conveniently, regardless of their location. The Central Election Commission announced this decision to guarantee the electoral rights of citizens residing or traveling abroad.

item.title: Uzbekistan Identifies Growth Points in Construction and Tourism Sectors
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with investors and entrepreneurs to discuss the development of the construction industry and tourism. A modern recreation zone was built in a short time, utilizing local enterprises for 95% of construction and equipment, reducing costs by 20%. The experience will be applied elsewhere, fostering synergy between construction and tourism.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Prime Minister Meets with World Bank and ADB Representatives
item.description: Prime Minister Adylbek Kasymaliev of Kyrgyzstan met with regional directors from the World Bank and Asian Development Bank (ADB) to discuss future cooperation and support for the country's socio-economic development priorities. Kasymaliev highlighted Kyrgyzstan's high economic growth rates and emphasized strengthening partnerships with international financial institutions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Builds Major Power Plant in Turkistan to Address Electricity Shortage
item.description: Kazakhstan is constructing a significant power plant in the Turkistan region as part of a strategy to achieve energy surplus by 2029. The "Turkistan" gas turbine plant, with a capacity of 1113.4 MW, aims to reduce electricity shortages in southern regions and ensure stable supply. Construction is 62% complete.

item.title: Turonbank Chairman Chori Mirzayev Reportedly Detained on Embezzlement Charges
item.description: Chori Mirzayev, who has led Turonbank since 2016, is reportedly under arrest. He is suspected of embezzling a large sum of money. Further details are expected.

item.title: ADB Finances Projects in Karakalpakstan, Focusing on Value Chains Beyond Roads
item.description: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) signed an updated memorandum of understanding with the Karakalpakstan government and is financing three projects in the region. ADB is Uzbekistan's second-largest creditor, aiming to support the country's development goals.

item.title: Rain and Black Ice Expected in Several Regions of Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan's western and northern regions are forecast to experience precipitation and black ice on November 21. Kazhydromet has released its weather predictions for all regions. Astana will be partly cloudy with no precipitation, while Almaty will also be partly cloudy without rain. Shymkent is expected to have rain and strong winds.

item.title: British Ambassador Visits Almalyk Mining and Metallurgical Combine in Uzbekistan
item.description: The British Ambassador to Uzbekistan, Timothy Smart, and representatives from Weir Minerals visited the Almalyk Mining and Metallurgical Combine (AGMK). The delegation toured the copper beneficiation plant and the mine, praising the facility's modern equipment and rapid construction. Discussions focused on future cooperation between AGMK and Weir Minerals, including implementing advanced technologies and improving operational efficiency.

item.title: Kuwaiti Fund to Finance Seven-Story Hospital Construction in Naryn, Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Representatives from the Arab Fund for Economic Development of Kuwait visited Kyrgyzstan to discuss cooperation and ongoing projects. A key focus was the planned construction of a seven-story hospital in Naryn, aimed at providing quality medical services to the region's residents. The fund expressed confidence in the hospital becoming a significant social facility.

item.title: Over 100 Trucks Congested at Kazakhstan-Russia Border Crossing in Kostanay Region
item.description: More than 100 trucks are backed up at the 'Kairak' border crossing point in the Kostanay region, Kazakhstan, bordering Russia. Drivers report waiting for days due to slow processing and ongoing reconstruction at the checkpoint. The Department of State Revenue attributes the congestion to reduced lane capacity during modernization efforts.

item.title: Kazakhstan President's 10 Key Development Principles Outlined
item.description: Vice President Yerlan Karin highlighted 10 significant principles from the President's speech on national development, state governance, and the rule of law. The focus includes agricultural development, improving rural well-being, and combating corruption.

item.title: Tashkent Water Utility Accused of Imposing Business Obligations on Property Owners
item.description: Tashkent's water utility is reportedly demanding property owners install electronic water meters with remote data transmission, even for non-residential spaces not used for business. This requirement is allegedly linked to obtaining a debt-free certificate needed for property sales. The utility's actions appear to extend beyond legal requirements for businesses.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Launch Special Platform for Local Construction Materials on State Procurement Portal
item.description: Uzbekistan will mandate the use of domestic construction materials for state-funded projects starting in 2027. A dedicated platform will be created on the state procurement portal to connect local producers with a market estimated at 15-20 trillion soms annually. The move aims to reduce construction costs and increase the use of local resources.

item.title: Migrant Boat Capsizes Off Senegal Coast, Several Feared Dead
item.description: A boat carrying dozens of migrants capsized near Yenne, Senegal, south of the capital Dakar. Local authorities reported the vessel, with at least 50 people aboard, hit a rock during a transfer from a smaller fishing boat. Four bodies were recovered by Thursday, according to an NGO representative.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches Initiative for Youth Safety and Mobility
item.description: Uzbekistan prioritizes creating conditions for youth development and education. The 'Safe Movement to School' project, supported by the 'Kelajak' Center and 'HAYOT' Foundation, donated a minibus to the Romitan district in Bukhara region to ensure safe routes to educational institutions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Adopts Comprehensive Approach to Child Welfare and Protection
item.description: Uzbekistan prioritizes child rights, welfare, and a secure future as a key state policy. Measures are in place to ensure the full development of the younger generation, including expanding educational opportunities and promoting inclusive education. The nation aims to provide a safe and nurturing environment for all children.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reports Significant Reduction in Three-Shift and Dilapidated Schools
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Education announced a substantial decrease in problematic schools, with only 36 operating on a three-shift basis and 27 classified as dilapidated. The majority of three-shift schools are in Almaty region, while dilapidated ones are concentrated in western Kazakhstan. The country is actively building new educational facilities to address these issues.

item.title: Bishkek Construction Company Fined and License Suspended for Premature Apartment Sales
item.description: A construction company in Bishkek had its license suspended and was fined 200,000 som for selling apartments before completing the building's underground levels. Regulations prohibit the sale of residential units and the collection of shared construction funds until the foundation and underground structure are finished. The company must rectify violations before resuming work.

item.title: Man Arrested for Groping Passenger on Astana Bus, Sentenced to 10 Days
item.description: A 33-year-old man in Astana was arrested and sentenced to 10 days of administrative detention for touching a female passenger inappropriately on a bus. The incident occurred after the victim warned him, and he then exited the bus. Police stated the man was intoxicated at the time of the offense and warned against public misconduct.

item.title: Court Orders Businessman to Demolish Illegal Two-Story Building in Taraz
item.description: A court in Taraz has ordered a businessman to demolish a two-story building constructed illegally, violating land use regulations and building codes. The structure was built without permits or proper documentation, despite previous warnings and fines. The court ruled the building a "self-built" structure.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Expedite Talks with Foreign Airlines on Fifth Freedom Rights
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to accelerate negotiations with foreign airlines regarding "fifth freedom" traffic rights. President Mirziyoyev emphasized expanding international air travel, noting interest from airlines like Turkish Airlines and Etihad. The country aims to facilitate easier access for travelers from regions currently requiring transit.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks in UN Top 20 for E-Government Development, Improving Digital Access
item.description: Kazakhstan has entered the UN's top 20 for e-government development, moving from 24th to 16th place. The country also significantly improved its mobile connectivity and internet access ranking, climbing 28 spots to 13th. "Kazakhtelecom" is expanding fiber-optic internet to rural areas, aiming to connect 3,008 villages by 2027.

item.title: Bus Driver Apprehended in Almaty for Operating with Forged Driver's License
item.description: A bus driver in Almaty was caught transporting passengers with a forged driver's license. Police discovered the fraudulent document after a bus accident in the Alatau district. The driver's license showed signs of crude manufacturing and was not found in the official database. The driver has been handed over for further investigation.

item.title: Underground Call Center in Tashkent Defrauded European Citizens Using Crypto Assets
item.description: Law enforcement in Tashkent has shut down an underground call center that defrauded European citizens. Ten individuals allegedly contacted Europeans via messengers, offering fake document services and trading courses. They used deceptive schemes to steal funds, converting them to cryptocurrency. Authorities seized equipment and are investigating crypto asset trafficking.

item.title: Four Convicted in Almaty for Fictitious Employment Scheme, State Losses Recovered
item.description: Four individuals have been convicted in Almaty for their involvement in a fictitious employment scheme that caused six million tenge in damages to the state. Two officials from the "Career Center of Almaty City" organized illegal salary payments for individuals who did not perform actual work. The state's losses have been fully compensated.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Teenager Convicted for Murdering and Burning Boyfriend's Body
item.description: A 15-year-old girl in Kazakhstan's Turkistan region has been convicted of murdering her boyfriend and burning his body. The incident occurred in May when the victim's body was found near an old factory. The girl, who had recently finished ninth grade, reportedly stabbed the 20-year-old multiple times after he refused to end their relationship.

item.title: Pavlodar Oncology Center Opens New Radiotherapy Unit with Advanced Linear Accelerator
item.description: The Pavlodar Regional Oncology Center has launched a new radiotherapy unit featuring a state-of-the-art linear accelerator and a CT simulator. The project, costing 3.2 billion tenge, aims to improve cancer treatment precision and reduce side effects. This upgrade aligns with national healthcare modernization goals.

item.title: 990 Trucks Stuck at Uzbekistan-Kazakhstan Border, Causing 40km Queue
item.description: A 40-kilometer queue of 990 trucks has formed at the B. Konysbayev border crossing between Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan. Drivers report waiting for several days to cross. The congestion is attributed to increased cargo flow from China via Kazakhstan and transit from Russia and Belarus. Uzbekistan is negotiating a 'One Stop' customs system with Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Malaysia to Resettle 10,000 Rohingya Refugees in Turkey Through Skills Training
item.description: Malaysia announced a program to resettle 10,000 Rohingya refugees currently in Malaysia to Turkey, providing them with skills training. This initiative, supported by Turkey, aims to offer a more coordinated and humane solution to the Rohingya situation.

item.title: Kazakh President Assigns Tasks to New National Security Committee Chairman
item.description: The President of Kazakhstan has given instructions to the newly appointed Chairman of the National Security Committee. The specific tasks and details of the instructions were not disclosed in the report.

item.title: China Purchases Monkeys for Experiments Amidst Global Competition
item.description: China has begun purchasing monkeys for its laboratory experiments, acquiring over 30,000 primates from Cambodia. This move intensifies a global race for research animals, following a previous US-Cambodia partnership that was halted due to a smuggling dispute. A new competition between the US and China is anticipated.

item.title: Thirty Families in Atyrau Receive Keys to New Apartments
item.description: Thirty families in Atyrau have received keys to new rental apartments with the right to purchase. The keys were presented by the regional governor and the chairman of "Otbasy Bank." The bank has programs supporting youth, medical workers, and rural residents, with 689 individuals housed since 2022.

item.title: Taliban Leader Describes Ghazni as Land of Saints and Martyrs
item.description: Taliban leader Hibatullah Akhundzada visited Ghazni province, calling it the 'cultural capital of Islam, land of saints, scholars, martyrs, and city of knowledge.' He emphasized obedience, administrative improvement, spreading knowledge, justice, and strengthening security. He also urged the reformation of youth through authentic Islamic and Afghan culture.

item.title: Tokayev Meets New National Security Chief, Gives Specific Instructions
item.description: President Tokayev met with the new Chairman of the National Security Committee, Marat Irmenov, to hear reports on ongoing national security work and future tasks. The meeting focused on reforming and increasing the efficiency of national security agencies. Tokayev also gave specific instructions regarding corruption prevention.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Tax Service Reports Top 5 Reforms in Five Years
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's tax revenues have nearly tripled in five years, reaching 308 billion soms in 2025 and exceeding 338 billion through October 2026. The State Tax Service highlighted five key reforms, including digitalization of services, new control methods, business support, and expanded benefits. Over 1.7 million users now utilize electronic tax services.
